newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish C.Bank source calls for tight budget policy.
newsitem.headline: Irish C.Bank source calls for tight budget policy.

text.p: A source close to the Central Bank has warned that budget policy needs to be tightened to ward off inflation and ensure that Ireland meets the price criteria for EMU, an agency report published in the Irish Independent said.

With the central bank's room to increase interest rates becoming more limited in the run-up to the creation of a single European currency, tightening fiscal conditions would be the best policy, the report said.
"This would reduce domestic demand without affecting the exchange rate. It is the best solution for borrowing to remain as low as possible," the source said.
A Central Bank spokesman declined to comment on the report.
There has been widespread speculation that Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn will announce significant tax reforms in his January budget.
The healthy state of Ireland's exchequer finances give him plenty of scope to cut taxes in the budget, the last before the next general election.
The budget is also being unveiled against the background of pay talks with both unions and employers demanding tax reform before they sign up for a new wage agreement.
But the central bank is known to be concerned about the high rate of domestic credit growth and the fact that Irish inflation is no longer among the lowest in the European Union.
It engineered a rise in Irish retail rates in late August but has seen fixed rate mortgage loans fall in recent days as overseas investors flooded into the Irish bond market, pushing yields down.
